# Line-coverage floor for the `coverage` CI job — the OFFLINE suite — in per cent.
#
# Enforced by `cargo run -p xtask -- coverage-ratchet`. One number; `#` comments and blank
# lines are ignored.
#
# The integration measurement has its own floor in `.github/coverage-floor-integration.txt`,
# taken by the `coverage-integration` job. The two numbers cover different test sets and are not
# comparable — never move a value from one file to the other.
#
# WHAT IT MEASURES. The job runs `cargo llvm-cov --workspace --all-targets` **without**
# `--features integration`, the same set every other fast job builds. So this is a floor on
# what the *offline* suite reaches, and it deliberately excludes the 118 `crates/db`, 86
# `services/api` and 55 `services/sync` integration tests, which need Docker and about fifteen
# minutes of migrations. Those are the sibling file's job.
#
# WHEN TO LOWER IT. There is one legitimate reason: code moved into a module the integration
# suites cover, so this number fell while the code got no less tested. Lower it in the same
# commit as the move and say so in the message.
#
# WHEN TO RAISE IT. Whenever the measured value has drifted a couple of points above it. The
# job prints the headroom and suggests a new value once there is enough, and since 2026-08-05
# also writes both to the run summary, so the suggestion is on the run page rather than buried
# in a log. A ratchet that only ever holds its original line stops being a ratchet.
#
# Baseline measured 2026-07-30 at 24.85% (regions 29.26%, functions 24.08%), set one point
# below to absorb `proptest`'s entropy-seeded runs — the one source of run-to-run variation in
# an otherwise deterministic measurement.
#
# Raised 2026-07-31 to 28.1, on the ratchet's own suggestion at 5.35 points of headroom.
# Re-measured at 29.15% (regions 33.78%, functions 27.67%) after TEST F-09's last axis landed:
# 31 `wiremock` tests over four HTTP clients that had no test below the trait boundary at all.
# Same one-point margin as the baseline, and the same reason for it.
#
# Not re-measured since 2026-07-31, across roughly twenty-five merged pull requests. A raise is
# likely owed and is deliberately not taken here: raising a ratchet to a figure nobody measured
# is the failure this file warns about above. Read the headroom the next `coverage` run prints
# and raise it to what that run suggests.
28.1
